bull.b: DAYBUE is showing strong volume-led growth while expanding geographically and through community practices. European approval, planned Japan submission, and substantial community headroom provide multiple durable avenues for patient and revenue growth beyond the current U.S. base.

Volume-driven NUPLAZID growth indicates continued underlying patient demand rather than reliance solely on pricing. Expanded physician coverage and stronger representative productivity can support broader adoption, helping extend the product’s commercial contribution over the next several quarters.

The shift to sustained profitability alongside low leverage gives ACADIA financial flexibility to fund clinical development and commercial investment internally. A stronger capital base also improves resilience as the company advances multiple pipeline programs and expands marketed products.

bear.b: The recent divergence between high net income and sharply lower free cash flow weakens confidence in earnings quality and operating consistency. If sustained, weaker cash conversion could reduce internally generated funding available for pipeline investment, launches, and strategic opportunities.

Missing the primary endpoint introduces meaningful uncertainty around remlifanserin’s development path in Alzheimer’s disease psychosis. Although the 60-milligram dose showed supportive secondary and safety findings, further trials and regulatory engagement remain necessary before this pipeline asset can contribute.

A decelerating revenue trajectory and less consistent operating profitability could make future earnings growth more dependent on execution from DAYBUE, NUPLAZID, and the pipeline. This reduces visibility into the durability of current earnings momentum despite positive reported net income.
